Drobin Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Drobin, Poland

Demolished. Drobin, granted town rights in 1511, saw Jewish settlement from the second half of the 17th century; by 1808, Jews made up over 90% of the population, still 45% (1,095 residents) by 1921. This older cemetery, founded in the mid-18th century near the synagogue complex and mikvah, remained in use into the second half of the 19th century. Germans converted the site into a military training ground during WWII, using all tombstones to pave streets; a sports field occupies the grounds today. A 1945 postwar murder of a Jewish family in nearby Raciąż discouraged the roughly 50-60 wartime survivors from returning to Drobin, effectively ending any chance of the community rebuilding.
